OMNI6-02Inadequate Gas Estimation Leads To Fund Theft From Memory Expansion Costs
AssetSolverNetOutbox.sol
StatusResolved: See Resolution
RatingSeverity: High Impact: High Likelihood: Medium
<|det|>title [68, 269, 178, 286]<|/det|>Description <|det|>text [66, 308, 930, 343]<|/det|>The function _fillGasLimit() is designed to estimate the gas required to mark an order as filled on the inbox. This gas is needed to cover the cost of executing the _fillHash() function on the source chain: <|det|>text [73, 359, 589, 530]<|/det|>function _fillHash(bytes32 orders0] internal view returns (bytes32) { SolverNet.Header memory header = orderHeader[orders0]; SolverNet.Call[] memory calls = _orderCalls[orders0]; SolverNet.TokenExports[] memory expenses = _orderExpenses[orders0]; SolverNet.fillOriginData memory fillOriginData = SolverNet.FillOriginData({ srcData = uint8(data[blockchain], destChainId: header.destChainId, fillDeadline: header.fillDeadline, calls: calls, expenses: expenses }); } return keccaks9(Abi.encode(orders0, abi.encode(fillOriginData))); } <|det|>text [67, 551, 930, 584]<|/det|>In this function, the data from _orderCalls[orderId] is loaded from storage into memory. However, the function _fillGasLimit() calculates the cost of loading from storage as follows: <|det|>text [73, 603, 648, 716]<|/det|>// 2500 gas for Call array length SLODD * dynamic cost of reading each call. uint256 callGas = 2500; for (uint256 i; i < fillData.calls.length; ++i) { SolverInit.call memory call = fillData.calls[i]; unchecked { // 5000 gas for the two slots that hold target, selector, and value. // 2500 gas per params slot (1 per function argument) used (minimum of 1 slot). callsGas += 5000 * (FixedPointMathLib.divipCall.params.length + 32, 32) + 2500); } } <|det|>text [65, 737, 933, 797]<|/det|>This cost estimate includes the gas for loading the call array length, as well as the gas for loading each call's parameters. However, it fails to account for memory expansion costs. For example, if the mstore opcode occupies 256 KB of memory space, the cost for memory expansion could be around 155,648 gas. This additional gas cost is not factored into the estimate, despite the 100K base gas being accounted for. <|det|>text [65, 808, 933, 899]<|/det|>This creates a vulnerability. If an attacker opens an order with a parameter length that is too large, after the order is filled on the destination chain and the attacker receives the tokens, the Solver will attempt to send a cross-rollup message via Omni Core to confirm the fulfillment. However, due to the underestimated gas in _fillGasLimit(), the transaction cannot be marked as filled on the source chain, as it requires more gas than expected. The function _fillHash() exceeds the estimated gas limit, preventing the Solver from marking the order as filled, and preventing the Solver from claiming the deposited amount. <|det|>footer [75, 924, 206, 945]<|/det|>sigma prime <|det|>page_number [820, 931, 881, 946]<|/det|>Page | 9

<PAGE><|det|>header [68, 60, 191, 73]<|/det|>Omni SolverNet
<|det|>header [751, 60, 882, 74]<|/det|>Detailed Findings
<|det|>text [65, 105, 930, 135]<|/det|>After the CLOSE_BUFFER period, the attacker can close the order and receive the deposited amount, even though the order was filled on the destination chain, leading to the theft of funds.
<|det|>text [67, 148, 631, 163]<|/det|>It is important to note that this scenario could also occur for order expenses.
<|det|>title [67, 196, 238, 212]<|/det|>Recommendations
<|det|>text [65, 235, 930, 264]<|/det|>A potential solution is to include the cost of memory expansion in the gas estimation within _fillGasLimit(), based on the Ethereum yellow paper:
<|det|>text [70, 279, 457, 293]<|/det|>Geometry * (max_memory / 32) + floor(max_memory[2 / 524,288])
<|det|>text [67, 313, 400, 328]<|/det|>Alternatively, a simplified approach could be:
<|det|>text [70, 344, 688, 358]<|/det|>callsGas += 3 * (call.params.length / 32) * (call.params.length + call.params.length / 524,288)
<|det|>title [67, 397, 169, 412]<|/det|>Resolution
<|det|>text [65, 436, 931, 480]<|/det|>The development team has addressed this issue by using the recommended formula to include gas costs for memory expansion. The Solady FixedPointMathLib mulDivUp and divUp functions were also incorporated to add a slight buffer to the computation.
<|det|>text [67, 493, 431, 508]<|/det|>This issue has been resolved in commit ea808d7.
<|det|>footer [73, 925, 206, 945]<|/det|>signal prime
<|det|>page_number [810, 931, 884, 946]<|/det|>Page | 10
